excludedAssessments.summary: The row-counting argument establishes D(77) <= 154, and the reproduced verifier is conditionally sound: a successful run on the supplied payload would establish a 152-point no-three-in-line configuration in the 76 x 76 grid and hence D(77) >= 152 by inclusion into the 77 x 77 grid. However, the bounded record contains neither trusted successful-execution evidence nor an independently checked exhaustive determinant trace. Thus the decisive noncollinearity predicate, the lower bound D(77) >= 152, and consequently the full interval 152 <= D(77) <= 154 remain unverified.

excludedAssessments.summary: The central rct4 encoding is statically plausible and appears sound and complete within its expressly defined subclass, and the half-turn/quarter-turn arguments are largely correct. However, the full declared contribution is not established: the claim that rct4 is the only rotational route overreaches because general central half-turn (rot2) configurations are not shown to satisfy the stricter rct4 conditions; the assertion that 153-point sets have no rotational symmetry omits the classification needed to exclude rotations other than half- and quarter-turns; and the numerical model count, certificate-validation results, and bounded solver runs are unsupported execution claims without trusted transcripts or objective attestation. These gaps do not supply a counterexample or refute the model, so the bounded record remains indeterminate.
scopeQualifications: Static reasoning supports soundness and completeness only for the defined rct4 subclass, not all half-turn-invariant 154-point configurations.

The symmetry lemma establishes the central half-turn envelope at size 154 only after restricting to the considered square-grid rotations; exclusion of all other planar rotational symmetries requires an omitted finite-order rational-rotation argument.
The bounded searches have no bearing on satisfiability, nonexistence, or the value of D(77).
The contribution does not alter the baseline interval 152 <= D(77) <= 154.
evidenceIssues: The statement that rct4 is the only rotational route is unsupported: rct4 imposes an empty anti-diagonal, full off-diagonal quarter-turn orbits, and one main-diagonal antipodal pair, none of which follows from central half-turn symmetry.
The conclusion that a 153-point set has no rotational symmetry at all omits an argument excluding rotational orders other than 2 and 4 or an explicit restriction to square-grid automorphisms.
The asserted count of 388,148 distinct constraints depends on execution and is not established by the prose alone.

Claims that all five calibration certificates pass, have the listed hashes, and satisfy the reported constraint counts lack a trusted execution transcript or terminal objective attestation; results.json is only claimed output.

The reported CP-SAT and CaDiCaL runs lack logs or content-addressed artifacts; the CaDiCaL invocation is unspecified, and the displayed n=77 command differs from the tabulated worker count and duration.

The prose that every maximal grid line contributes a constraint is literally imprecise because tautological lines are omitted and equivalent expressions are deduplicated, though this does not appear to impair model correctness.

excludedAssessments.summary: Static source-level analysis supports the subclass encoding and line-constraint semantics: there are 1,444 four-cell off-diagonal rotation orbits and 38 main-diagonal antipodal pairs; selecting 38 orbit variables and one pair variable gives 154 points; and the weighted maximal-line inequalities are sound and complete for the no-three-in-line condition within the explicitly defined subclass. However, the material assertions that canonical deduplication yields exactly 388,148 constraints and that the serialization has SHA-256 digest 5c0051739717f52f8eddd00cd01e8a83030849b3fd7b4516b0d308882c9aaf62 are not established by trusted execution, a supplied complete serialization, or equivalent evidence. No contradiction or counterexample was found, so the claim remains indeterminate rather than invalid.
